# THE EXPORT TIER'S TRIGGER: a pull request that changes a path matching any line below runs the
# export-video tests (CTest LABELS export, tests/CMakeLists.txt); one that changes none leaves them
# out, and the run's summary says so by name. Pushes to main, tags, manual and weekly runs always
# run them. Owner ruling 2026-11-18: "run the slow export tests only when export code changes,
# always on main".
#
# A false "run" costs minutes; a false "skip" lets a broken export reach main. So the list is
# CONSERVATIVE and checked: tests/test_ci_tiers.py walks every import of every export-labelled test,
# transitively, and fails when a file in that closure matches no line here. On 2026-11-18 the
# closure held 91 of the 93 app modules (all but studio/__main__.py and studio/gearing.py:
# studio/session.py alone imports coaching, stats and focus, and five of the suites import
# studio/app.py), so the app is one line rather than a module list that would rot.
#
# Syntax: one glob per line, `*` is the only wildcard and it matches across `/` (bash `[[ == ]]`,
# Python fnmatch: .github/export-tier.sh and the test read it the same way). `#` starts a comment.

# What every test runs on: the build, the C++ core and its bindings, the environment, CI itself.
.github/*
CMakeLists.txt
pyproject.toml
pixi.lock
pacer/*
bindings/*
3rdparty/*

# The app: every module (the dev tools included: the tests build their fixtures with them), and
# the fonts and data files the painter and the loader read.
studio/*.py
studio/*.json
studio/assets/*

# The export tests themselves, the shared helpers they import, and how CTest and pytest run them.
tests/test_export_*.py
tests/_*.py
tests/conftest.py
tests/pytest.ini
tests/CMakeLists.txt
tests/test_ci_tiers.py
